newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa's Mossgas in joint venture talks.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Mossgas in joint venture talks.

text.p: South African fuel-from-gas producer Mossgas is engaged in "promising" talks with unnamed potential partners interested in chemicals and offshore natural gas exploration, chief executive David Day said on Monday.

"There are some very interesting prospects on both the chemicals onshore and on the gas exploration offshore, and discussions are extremely promising. Watch this space," Day told the Africa Oil conference here.

He said the Central Energy Fund and state-run exploration company Soekor had been instructed to pursue the possibility of joint ventures and strategic equity alliances in respect of further exploration for gas and its exploitation.

The Mossgas plant, producing 30,000 barrels a day of liquid fuel from offshore gas, was offered for privatisation earlier this year. But the exercise fell flat with the government rejecting all bids and terminating the privatisation process at the end of June.
The Mossgas project, designed to boost South African energy self-sufficiency, has been crticised as a white elephant of the apartheid era.
Built at a cost of 11.4 billion rand which was way over budget, it was also found to have proven reserves amounting to only 13 years consumption.
